entityDescription:
 Company history

Created in 1986, MAP was born from the meeting between the CNES “Materials” research laboratory, intended to design coatings for the space environment and to ensure production, and Maestria, a painting company in the south of France, near Toulouse.
Since its creation, MAP has been able to respond, through its products and services (hot or cold coatings, compliant coatings, adhesives, greases, etc.), to the technical, strategic and financial challenges of the space sector. 
Today, MAP is one of the 20 SMEs in the space sector, with CNES having entered into a "winning partnership", within the framework of the SME Pact. 

 Description of activities (main and / or secondary) 

MAP specializes in the design, manufacture and application of thermal finish coatings for satellites and launchers. 

 Description of products and / or services and sectors of application

 The coatings offered by MAP are the result of the unique know-how and expertise of the R&D department and thus meet the needs of the space industry. MAP therefore offers a rich and varied range of coatings: 
• Satellite thermal control coatings 
• Adhesives for satellite 
• Compliant coatings for satellite electronics 
• Lubricants for the satellite mechanisms 
• Thermal and electrical control coatings for launcher

Beyond the design and manufacture of coatings, MAP's know-how also relates to their characterization and application. This is how the company has:

• A physico-chemical characterization service, which covers mechanical, thermomechanical, rheological, thermo-optical, degassing and electrical characterizations; 
• An application service: the application of thermal control coatings on satellite parts being a critical phase, it requires a perfect mastery of the coating application techniques. 

Thanks to in-depth knowledge of its coatings and its experience in the treatment of satellite parts (more than 5,000 parts per year), MAP thus offers its customers the application of thermal control coatings on satellite parts, and training in application, repair of coatings as well as bonding of OSRs.

entityDescription:
D+T Microelectrónica, A.I.E. is an Association of Economic Interest charged with managing the functioning of CNM's Clean Room, placing within reach of industry microelectronic solutions that follow the cycle Design - Development - Production. The mission of D+T Microelectrónica, A.I.E. is to facilitate the incorporation of microelectronic technologies in industrial products, designing, developing and manufacturing chips tailored to specific needs. The Clean Room at CNM and the infrastructure existing on the site at Bellaterra (Barcelona) offer industry, and, in particular, small and medium-sized enterprises, the opportunity to introduce microelectronic technology into their products. The areas of design and testing, coupled with the production of chips in silicon technology, enable the manufacture of integrated circuits, special devices and microsystems tailored to their needs. The evolution, from conventional electronics to microelectronic technology, is a valuable alternative that enables industry to achieve the performance and costs necessary to keep their products competitive. Microelectronic technology assists in obtaining extra added value which enables improvements in the competitiveness of their products and, in some cases, assures the future viability of the same.

The Spanish National Research Council (CSIC) is its majority partner and its industrial partners are: Mondragón Componentes S. Coop, Agbar (Sociedad General de Aguas de Barcelona S.A.) and Alter Technology Ventures, S.L.

entityDescription:
For 30 years MediaMobil is providing satellite and radio communications services for maritime, offshore and land customers. The company operates a state-of-the-art VSAT network. Via teleports located in Europe and the US global connectivity is offered for Internet Access, telephony, corporate network connectivity, Cloud services, teleconferencing and any other data, voice or video applications.
Our main teleport and Network Operation Center (NOC) is located at Bremen near to the major European sea ports and close to the Northern and Baltic Sea regions. Being part of the critical network infrastructure in Germany, the teleport is fully redundant and qualified for services with highest availability and security requirements, both for government and commercial users. 
Operating an own physical network, MediaMobil has complete control of the end-to-end connections and can monitor and manage the services independently from third parties. The aim is to provide each customer a service package which is tailored to their specific needs including hardware and airtime. 
MediaMobil is extending its portfolio of geostationary (GEO) satcom services by the new Low and Medium Earth Orbit (LEO/MEO) satellite systems OneWeb and O3b mPOWER. The multi-orbit services are integrated via an intelligent Multi Link Gateway (MLG) - designed and manufactured inhouse - providing a fully managed service to the customer. The MLG also integrates Starlink services. 
The overall Scope of Work and Services includes:
* Design of customized telecommunications solutions for global use
* Supply, installation and commissioning of hardware and software
* Global maintenance and repair
* 24/7 network operation and customer support
* Development of hardware and software for special customer needs
Our goal is to offer our customers exactly the services and solutions they need. We use all our expertise and our network to achieve this. Because the success of our customers is also our success. 
MediaMobil also pays special attention to cyber security. From the conception and operation of holistic security systems to the protection of individual applications and components, MediaMobil implements an IT security framework based on the guidelines of the German Federal Office for Information Security (BSI).
Besides of the commercial activities, MediaMobil participates in R&D programs with the objective to develop innovative satcom solutions such as communications systems for remote control of tug boats and for Unmanned Vehicles (UUVs/UAVs).
MediaMobil is also member of the German Offshore Spaceport Alliance (https://www.offshore-spaceport.de/en/). GOSA is developing an offshore launch platform for small and medium size rockets. MediaMobil oversees the communications network to interconnect the launch-, control- and guard vessels in the offshore launch area using advanced private 5G (P5G) network technology integrated with high speed satcom systems.
MediaMobil is authorized dealer and service partner of the major satcom system manufacturers Cobham, Intellian, Kymeta and ST Engineering (iDirect). The company is also certified to provide Voice-over-IP (VoIP) telephony solutions.
Maintenance and repair services are provided by own engineers as well as a global network of partners certified by the system manufacturers.
MediaMobil reference customers include major deep sea and offshore shipping companies, research institutes, construction companies, power grid operators and government authorities with worldwide operations.

entityDescription:
Brockmann Consult GmbH (BC) is a private company, founded in 2002, offering scientific consultancy and environmental informatics services. The company is actively involved in Earth Observation data management, processing and QC, and software development. Brockmann Consult is led by Dr. Carsten Brockmann, a physical oceanographer, who has been working now for 20 years in optical remote sensing and software development. The company has presently 30 employees including software engineers, physicists and environmental scientists, all with a sound and long term software development experience and project management.
Brockmann Consult has two branches: Environmental Informatics and Geoinformation Services, which complement each other. The objective of the Geoinformation Services group is the provision of custom-made information products and consultancy services, connected with environmental data. This includes scientific consultancy for environmental concerns, data processing and QC services and value-added products and thematic information derived from remote sensing data. The products range from mosaics of satellite images to qualitative and quantitative information concerning the environment. BC serves local and global applications with focus on the marine and coastal environment. The objective of Environmental Informatics is the development of custom-made software solutions for environmental data. Important products include the BEAM toolbox, the ESA reference solution for visualisation, analysis and processing of optical Earth Observation data which will also form the basis for the Copernicus Sentinel 1, 2 and 3 toolboxes, Calvalus, a high performance processing system, that fulfils the needs of rapid improvement, development, processing and validation of Earth Observation data products and MERCI database system for organisation and processing of large satellite image archives.
The focus of the activities of Brockmann Consult is on system development projects for Earth Observation Processing Systems. As a major activity, Brockmann Consult has been and is deeply involved in the preparation, quality control and evolution of software for the processing of MERIS data. BC is concerned with details of the MERIS products and its generation, which has lead to a deep understanding of the scientific algorithms, and particularly the ENVISAT, ERS and future Sentinel product formats.

Company description: BIC Lazio, founded in 1990 by the Latium Region with Regional Law 35/90, is the regional network agency responsible for encouraging local development through the promotion of an entrepreneurial culture and support the creation and development of business initiatives. 

BIC Lazio belongs to the European BIC Network (EBN) and the European Association of Development Agencies (EURADA). Since 2003 it hosts the Euro Information Centre IT 389. BIC Lazio activities include: 
-	promotion of entrepreneurial culture;
-	support to local actors in choosing development strategies to enhance local resources and in taking part in European Programmes; 
-	support for enterprise creation; 
-	assistance to SMEs in pinpointing development opportunities; 
economic exploitation of research findings (spin-offs from academic and research work) in collaboration with Universities and Research centres. 

BIC Lazio holds five incubators in the region and in 2006 set up ITech, the incubator for the promotion and creation of new enterprises engaged in high tech activities. It is located in Tecnopolo Tiburtino of Rome, in cooperation with the company of Polo Tecnologico Industriale Romano. The incubator provides integrated and detailed services of pre-incubation and incubation, able to turn ideas, research projects and experiences from productive system into new business. The process of business support is divided in four phases: scouting of new business innovative ideas; selection; pre-incubation assistance; incubation.

At the moment, the programme ITech Spazio is active and founds itself on an Agreement between BIC Lazio and ESA (European Space Agency), aimed to the identification of ESA¿s skills and competences which offer a potential industrial exploitation for no space application and to the definition of the tools for the transfer of those competencies.

entityDescription:
Andøya Space Education (ASE), is a national center for all educational levels within space education in Norway. The main activities are linked to Andøya Space. ASE is a subsidiary company of Andøya Space and is partly funded by the Norwegian Ministry of Education and Research. ASE initiates, develops, and performs educational activities, seminars and conferences at all levels of education within subject areas related to space, such as space technology, space physics, atmosphere and environment.

The organisation Andøya Space Education (former known as NAROM), partly supported by the Norwegian Government, was formed in year 2000 to organise space education and ensure recruiting, promote appreciation for the benefits of space activities, and to stimulate the interest for science in general.

Andøya Space Education main task is to ensure recruitment to Norwegian Space industry and to increase the interest for Science and Technology. This is done to some extend by:
-
Develop and perform educational activities using the unique infrastructure at Andøya Space.
-
Ensure recruitment to Norwegian space industry by developing space-related courses and Secondary level, at University level, initiate, perform national, and international space related educational projects.
-
Increase the interest and the competence for STEM by offering professional and in-formal teacher training courses for teachers and teacher students at primary and secondary level. Develop space related resources and arrange seminar and excursions for pupils and teachers.
-
Increase the knowledge about why space is important and useful in the context of earth and climate. 
-
Increase the space industry in the northern region as part of the government’s strategy for the high North.
-
Develop and perform educational activities in different regions with a strong link to the relevant curriculum in the schools.
-
Establish a stronger position for Norway within international collaboration about space education.
